scenes.title: United States
scenes.subtitle: A history told only by its sources

scenes.caption: Photo 1898
scenes.text: Tensions between the colonies and British authorities subsequently intensified, leading to the Revolutionary War, which commenced with the Battles of Lexington and Concord on April 19, 1775.

scenes.caption: Photo 1901
scenes.text: On September 3, 1783, in the Treaty of Paris, the British acknowledged the independence and sovereignty of the Thirteen Colonies, leading to the establishment of the United States.

scenes.caption: Photo 1902
scenes.text: In the 1788–89 presidential election, Washington was elected the nation's first president.

scenes.caption: Photo 1901 · New York
scenes.text: In 1624, after years of disease and Indian attacks, including the Powhatan attack of 1622, King James I revoked the Virginia Company's charter and made Virginia a royal colony.

scenes.caption: Photo 1902 · New York
scenes.text: Native American attacks continued, with the most significant occurring in the 1637 Pequot War and the 1675 King Philip's War.

scenes.caption: Photo 1901 · New York
scenes.text: The British Parliament passed the Stamp Act of 1765, imposing a tax on the colonies without going through the colonial legislatures.

scenes.caption: Photo 1898
scenes.text: In upstate New York, a major British invasion of New York State was repelled at the Battle of Plattsburgh, and Jackson decisively defeated another invasion at the Battle of New Orleans in early 1815.

scenes.caption: Photo 1901
scenes.text: The Missouri Compromise was repealed in 1854 with the Kansas–Nebraska Act; promoted by Stephen Douglas in the name of "popular sovereignty" and democracy, this act of Congress permitted voters to decide on the legality of slavery…

scenes.caption: Photo 1902
scenes.text: In perhaps the turning point of the war, Lee's army was badly beaten by the Army of the Potomac, and in July 1863, the Union's victory at the Battle of Gettysburg in Pennsylvania, the deadliest battle in American military history…

scenes.title: What the sources leave out
scenes.text: Before 1624, history is not dated in these sources: oral traditions, archaeology and local sources are still to be brought in.
